newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsubishi Corp says trading safeguards in place.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi Corp says trading safeguards in place.

text.p: The president of Japanese trade house Mitsubishi Corp said on Thursday his firm has no plans to tighten its trading procedures following Sumitomo Corp's $2.6 billion loss due to unauthorised copper trades.

"I must admit I did ask our metals people about this after it happened, but Mitsubishi is not moving to put more safeguards in place. I think the systems already in place are pretty good," Minoru Makihara told Reuters.
"Sumitomo made a basic mistake in combining the back office and front office functions in one person," he said.
Makihara, speaking after a news conference, said Mitsubishi is likely to expand its activities in commodities in the future.
"We're thinking about it (expanding in commodities). The resources area will inevitably become more important to Mitsubishi in the future because there are going to be more shortages," he said.
He said while Mitsubishi was already fairly big in the oil and gas sectors, it was also looking at fertilisers and food.
